screen: Public homepage, business section (phone 390), Stage 6 pass 2

expected_differences: Demo Coffee Co., Jasmine Reed and Raleigh are production-account content; they should not be replaced with the Lab’s Loopday, Maya and Austin fixtures.
Content shows “The slow pour.” with “Edit requested” and four delivered files, rather than the Lab’s “Counter reset,” “New” and five-file fixture. Preserve the production state.
Essential at $99/month and Growth at $199/month are legitimate configured prices. Their shoot, photo and video allocations remain explicitly stated.

The production Home, Create, Story-proof review and Content captures legitimately replace the Lab’s fixture demonstrations. Their actual records and states—not the Lab’s default selections—are the functional reference.
keep: Mineral canvas, strong Archivo headings, restrained cobalt, exact-looking lockup and graphite device housings without ambient shadows.
The campaign-to-monthly-content sequence: discovery, campaign creation and review establish a working platform rather than a generic subscription pitch.
Real product captures and the clearly labeled Inspect actions. Do not replace them with fabricated UI or force the Lab’s page layout onto this implementation.
The explicit generated-sample disclosure beside monthly content, separate from the production Content capture.
Visible plan allocations, subscription prices and the clear statement that campaign credit funds work separately from the content subscription.
review.readiness_note: The capture exposes the real business workflows and entry actions; it does not demonstrate broken application functionality. Hold visual sign-off for the fixes below, then verify strip navigation and Inspect dialogs at 390px, including readable enlargement, Close, Escape and focus return.

drift.change: Add visible Previous and Next buttons outside the campaigns overflow strip, between the strip and its inspection links. Use minimum 44×44px targets, IBM Plex Sans 14/20px status text and an initial “Step 1 of 3” label. Advance one capture per activation, update the step on native swiping and disable the appropriate endpoint button. Retain the intentional right-edge preview.
drift.why: The complete campaigns assembly shows Home, a clipped Create frame and three Inspect buttons, but no Previous, Next or step indicator. The later review frame is named without a visible browsing control. The intentional clipping is not the defect; undisclosed strip position is.
drift.where: Campaigns phone strip, immediately above the grouped provenance caption and Inspect Home/Create/review buttons.

drift.change: Attach a native caption to each product figure using IBM Plex Sans 14/20px, directly below its capture and associated with its Inspect action. Populate account, screen and literal state from that capture’s metadata. Home can read “Demo product · Demo Coffee Co. · Business Home · 4 campaign decisions · 2 files to approve”; Content can read “Demo product · Demo Coffee Co. · Content · The slow pour. · Edit requested.” Give Create and Review their own captions without inventing an unseen review outcome. Keep the generated-shoot disclosure separately attached to the sample images.
drift.why: Pass 2’s per-frame provenance and readable states are not visible here. Campaigns has one collective “Demo account · Production screens…” caption; Content names the screen but omits its file state. Demo disclosure is present and honest, but operational states remain inside miniature screenshots.
drift.where: Captions beneath the campaigns frames and the monthly Content/sample assembly.

drift.change: Remove the decorative horizontal rules below Essential and Growth: set the plan-row and spending-note borders to 0, with no replacement pseudo-element separator. Keep the regions square and shadowless; use a 12px gap between plan rows and 24px before the campaign-spending note.
drift.why: Thin full-width rules remain beneath both plan prices despite the approved unboxed plan treatment and the stated pass-2 border removal. Typography and spacing already distinguish these short records.
drift.where: Essential/Growth plan list, including the rule immediately above “Campaign spending is separate…”

review.why: The foundation is convincingly Frame Shift: restrained surfaces, substantial typography, recognizable branding and authentic product screens carry the business story. Campaign funding and monthly shoots are understandable, and prices are not presented as creator earnings. The remaining failures are local implementation details, not grounds for another art direction. No additional decorative source-to-decision notch belongs on these plan rows. Repeated headers and broad seams are composite-capture artifacts, and the intentionally clipped later strip items are not themselves responsive drift. Other homepage chapters and the complete Get paid region are outside this capture’s review scope.
review.verdict: The business section preserves TapMart’s real workflows and largely carries Frame Shift, but missing strip controls, grouped state captions and residual plan rules prevent sign-off on this phone pass.
